title: Human-ceiling annotation record
description: One independent digitization of one figure already in data/verified_pairs/registry.json (status=verified), used to score inter-annotator agreement ("human ceiling") -- see data/human_ceiling/FORMAT.md for the full explanation, and src/real_chart_bench/adapter/human_ceiling_annotations.py for the authoritative parser/validator this document mirrors.

paper_id.description: Must match a paper_id in data/verified_pairs/registry.json.

figure_id.description: Must match a figure_id in data/verified_pairs/registry.json for the given paper_id. Combined with paper_id as '{paper_id}-{figure_id}' to key results, matching every other results/*.json's per_figure figure_id convention.

annotation_source.description: MANDATORY, never defaulted. 'human' = a person manually re-digitized the figure (e.g. WebPlotDigitizer). 'llm' = a large language model produced the digitization. 'automated' = a non-LLM automated pipeline (e.g. a CV extraction tool) produced it. Only a set of annotations that are ALL 'human' may ever be labeled/published as a 'human ceiling' -- see domain.human_ceiling.require_human_ceiling(). A missing or unrecognized value is a hard parse error, not a default.

annotator_id.description: Identity of the annotator/system, e.g. a person's handle for a human annotation, or a model/tool identifier for llm/automated (e.g. 'gpt-4o-digitizer-v1'). Never left blank.

annotated_at.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) the digitization was produced.

tool.description: Optional. The digitization tool used, e.g. 'WebPlotDigitizer 4.7'.

notes.description: Optional free-text notes (ambiguous series, uncertain calibration, etc.).

curves.description: One entry per data series digitized in this annotation.

series_label.description: Optional. Should match/approximate the corresponding ground_truth.json series' prop_y or legend label where identifiable, to help pair series across annotations.
